title: Pampas Grass Removed - Gravel Garden Added

seo.title: Gravel Garden & Patio Transformation in Newquay
seo.description: See how I transformed an overgrown garden in Newquay, Cornwall by removing pampas grass and creating a low-maintenance gravel garden with a fresh patio area.
seo.ogTitle: Before & After: Gravel Garden with Patio (Newquay)
seo.ogDescription: Pampas grass removed and replaced with a tidy, low-maintenance gravel garden and patio. A clean, modern outdoor space built to last.

hero.imageAlt: Brand new gravel garden with new patio

overview.label: Project overview
paragraphs: This Newquay garden had been taken over by a large pampas grass that dominated the whole space. It was one of those situations where a single plant had been left to do its own thing for too long, and everything around it had suffered. The borders were overgrown, the ground beneath was a mess, and the homeowner could not really use any of the garden. They wanted the pampas gone and something low-maintenance in its place, with a proper area for sitting outside.

Removing established pampas grass is not a five-minute job. The root systems are dense and deep, and in the Cornish climate where growth is vigorous, a mature clump can be substantial. I cut the foliage back first, then dug out the root ball and cleared the surrounding vegetation. Green waste removal was agreed at £10 per dumpy bag; Quilliams is an Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202. There was a fair amount to shift on this one.

With the site cleared, I levelled the ground across the full area and laid heavy-duty weed membrane. The membrane is critical for any gravel garden that is going to last, particularly in Cornwall where mild, damp winters encourage growth year-round. I pinned everything down properly at joins and edges, then spread decorative gravel over the top for a clean, even surface.

The patio element of this project made a real difference to how the homeowner could use the garden. I prepared a solid base and laid paving slabs to create a dedicated seating area. Having a proper hard surface for a table and chairs turned what had been an unusable space into somewhere they could actually sit and enjoy. The patio connects neatly to the gravel, with clean edging separating the two surfaces.

The budget for a gravel garden with patio installation in Cornwall typically falls in the £1,500 to £2,500 range, depending on the size of the patio, the amount of clearance needed, and the materials chosen. This project was completed over a few days. The difference between before and after was dramatic. From a garden dominated by one out-of-control plant to a clean, practical, modern outdoor space.

faq.question: How long does a gravel garden transformation take?
faq.answer: Most gravel garden projects take between two and four days, depending on the amount of clearance needed, access to the site, and whether patio works are included. A straightforward clearance and gravel job can be done in two days. Adding a patio adds another day or so. I confirm timings after a site visit or once I have seen photos of the space.

faq.question: Will weeds grow through the gravel?
faq.answer: A properly installed weed membrane stops almost all growth from below. The only weeds you will see are surface ones from wind-blown seeds, and these pull out easily because they are sitting on gravel rather than rooting into soil. In Cornwall, where the mild climate keeps things growing longer than most parts of the UK, good ground preparation and quality membrane are especially important. I use heavy-duty membrane and pin it carefully at every join.

faq.question: How do I maintain a gravel garden?
faq.answer: Gravel gardens need very little upkeep. An occasional rake to redistribute the surface, clearing fallen leaves in autumn, and pulling the odd weed is about it. Some homeowners top up the gravel every two to three years to refresh the appearance, but this is cosmetic rather than structural. Compared to a lawn or planted beds, the time saving is significant.

faq.question: Can you add a patio or path as part of the project?
faq.answer: Yes, I regularly combine gravel gardens with patio areas, stepping stone paths, or defined edging. Adding a hard surface for seating makes a real difference to how usable the garden is. I prepare a proper base for any paving to make sure it stays level and drains well. The cost depends on the size and materials, but I include it all in a single clear quote.
